title: Simple, fast, and accurate methodology for quantitative analysis using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, with bio-hybrid fuel cell examples
author: Mackie, Jahnke, et al.

steps.title: Prepare computer and software
steps.instruction: Install the MPLM Visual Basic program on a laptop equipped with a 2.66 GHz Intel Core2 Duo CPU, 4 GB RAM, running 64‑bit Windows 7; ensure Microsoft Visual Basic 2010 is available.

steps.title: Configure mesh parameters
steps.instruction: In the MPLM interface set the first‑pass concentration mesh step size (s1) to 10 % (bounded between 0 % and 50 %); set the backing‑off factor (B) to 0.8 steps; set the mesh‑size reduction factor (r) to 4 so that each subsequent step size si+1 = si × B / r = si / 5; allow up to 9 passes; the program will stop refining when the step size falls below 0.01 %.

steps.title: Prepare water background
steps.instruction: Fill the FTIR sample compartment with deionized water and record a background spectrum; repeat this water‑background measurement immediately before measuring each component spectrum and each sample spectrum.

steps.title: Acquire component spectra
steps.instruction: Prepare solutions of each pure component at several concentrations that roughly match the expected concentrations in the unknown mixtures; for each concentration record an FTIR spectrum using the water background just obtained.

steps.title: Acquire sample spectrum
steps.instruction: Prepare the aqueous mixture sample and record its FTIR spectrum using a freshly measured water background.

steps.title: Fit sample with MPLM
steps.instruction: Load the sample spectrum and the set of component spectra into the MPLM program; run the multi‑pass LAMR algorithm with the parameters defined in step 2 to obtain component percentages that minimize the RMS error εRMS (Equation 2); if any initial concentration guess differs by more than 15 % from the fitted value, repeat the fit using component spectra measured at concentrations closer to the new estimate.

steps.title: Optional SMM for two components
steps.instruction: For mixtures containing only two components, run the brute‑force single‑mesh method (SMM) by evaluating εRMS for all concentration combinations with a mesh step of 0.1 %; on the specified computer this yields 0.1 % precision in about 15 minutes.

steps.title: Record computational parameters
steps.instruction: Note that the MPLM program is coded for up to 9 passes and can handle up to 9 mixture components plus a background component; with the chosen parameters the mesh step size decreases from 10 % at pass 1 to 10 %/58 ≈ 0.000026 % at pass 9, but the program stops refining when the step size falls below 0.01 %; the single‑mesh method (SMM) evaluates εRMS for every concentration combination and for two‑component mixtures achieves 0.1 % precision in ≈15 min on a laptop with a 2.66 GHz Intel Core2 Duo CPU, 4 GB RAM, running 64‑bit Windows 7; the reduction factor η for MPLM versus SMM is given by η = (100/0.01) N 9 × 10^N ≈ 10^5 N 10 × 10^N = 10^4 N − 1 (Equation 3).
